PreToolUse.description: Gate AskUserQuestion: block (exit 2) when options lack a clearly-marked recommendation + reason; agent must re-issue with both. Tiered LLM judge (GLM → Anthropic API → claude -p subscription; see hooks/lib/llm-judge.js) reads tool_input.questions directly; fail-open on no-backend/error/timeout. Enforces CLAUDE.md 'Surface Choices (Real Ones), Recommend One'.

Block (exit 2) a codeagent-wrapper dispatch with no stdin source: the wrapper reads its own stdin before launching the backend, so with no EOF it hangs silently for ~20 minutes with zero output and no completion callback. Fix is `</dev/null` (prompt is an argument) or a heredoc / pipe / `-` form. Allow-biased: any `<` anywhere, any help/version flag, and every ambiguous shell form fail open. Set CODEAGENT_STDIN_GUARD=0 to disable. Enforces references/background-agent-monitoring.md '派发前自限'.

Register the writer and block overlapping concurrent edits (references/concurrent-plan-isolation.md 「轻量登记」). The registry lives in the git common-dir, not the worktree, so entries written from one worktree are visible from every other; the hook writes, reads AND expires entries, because the observed failure was not 'nobody registers' but 'entries are written, never read, never cleaned'.

Block pattern-matched process killing (pkill / killall): they select victims by name or command line, so one call reaches processes owned by other concurrent agent sessions, and the caller sees nothing wrong. `kill <pid>` has no such reach and stays allowed. Motivating incident (2026-08-07): `pkill -f agent-browser` killed every agent-browser daemon on the box, not just the wedged one.

Enforce create-commit's commit-message language rule (English by default; exceptions are an explicit user request, a repo whose recent history is Chinese, or a term with no accurate English equivalent). Purely deterministic (scan characters + read git log). It exists because the rule was in context and still lost once: the turn that wrote the message followed a long stretch of editing Chinese docs and the body drifted along with it.

Stop.description: Desktop notification when Claude finishes responding: Ghostty OSC9 (clicking focuses the originating tab) with terminal-notifier as fallback elsewhere. Replaces the ECC plugin's stop:desktop-notify (disabled via ECC_DISABLED_HOOKS) so the logic lives in version control, not a third-party plugin cache.

Block a stop whose closing line promises a follow-up action (「接下来我做 X」) while nothing is actually running — no task, monitor, or subagent. To the caller that sentence is simply false. The existing gates cannot see it: stop-gate.js judges whether the USER was asked to act, and this failure asks nothing of the user, so it falls outside that axis entirely.

Block a stop that hands the user a set of parallel options as a prose list instead of via AskUserQuestion — the carrier half of CLAUDE.md 'Surface Choices'. ask-recommend-gate structurally cannot fire here (it is PreToolUse on AskUserQuestion, and the whole failure is that the call never happened), and stop-gate correctly passes it, since 'asking the user to decide' is an explicit ok clause in its rubric.

Block a stop asserting that a named tool is unavailable / uncallable in this session when it was never actually called. The session-opening deferred-tools snapshot is a NEGATIVE capability claim that expires and is never retracted, and negative claims are not self-falsifying — whoever believes it will not try the call. Real consequences twice: an unverified 'cannot TaskStop' left 6 dead teammates unreclaimed and shipped that reason to the user.

Block a stop that delivers a reverse assertion (X does not exist / is not authorized / is unavailable / is a dead end) when the reading behind it would look identical were the claim false. Accepting one deletes the checks that should have followed: a positive misjudgment gets caught downstream, a reverse one has no downstream. Real case (2026-08-07): 'this host's SSH key is not authorized' — the actual cause was a non-interactive shell missing SSH_AUTH_SOCK.

Before stopping, put long-unaccounted-for background shells in front of the agent. From a real incident: three `until ! pgrep -f pytest` loops spun for 15 hours (pgrep -f matched the loop's own command line, so the condition never cleared) while the agent repeatedly announced 'cleanup complete, nothing pending'. stop-gate.js has the right timing but reads only the last assistant message, so it sees zero process facts.
